shows.name: Demon Slayer
shows.description: Demon Slayer is set in Taisho-era Japan (1912–1926). Almost every location in the show is inspired by real places you can visit.

spots.name: Asakusa, Tokyo
spots.subtitle: Taisho-era streets of the show
spots.description: The preserved Taisho-era streets of Asakusa are the direct visual inspiration for Demon Slayer's world. Walking through Nakamise-dori at dawn feels like stepping into the anime. The stone lanterns, wooden shopfronts, and Senso-ji temple gates are unmistakably Tanjiro's Japan.

spots.name: Gion District, Kyoto
spots.subtitle: The soul of Demon Slayer's world
spots.description: Gion's hanamikoji street — with its wooden machiya townhouses, stone-paved alleys, and paper lanterns — is the atmosphere Demon Slayer is built on. At dusk, with geisha occasionally passing, it feels exactly like the show. This is the must-see Demon Slayer location.

spots.name: Fushimi Inari, Kyoto
spots.subtitle: 1,000 torii gates — Final Selection forest
spots.description: The dense forest of vermillion torii gates climbing the mountain at Fushimi Inari directly echoes the forests of Demon Slayer — particularly the Final Selection arc on Mt. Fujikasane. Going at dawn means misty, atmospheric photos with almost no crowds.

spots.name: Ashikaga Flower Park, Tochigi
spots.subtitle: Wisteria forest — Final Selection arc
spots.description: Ashikaga's Great Wisteria — a 160-year-old wisteria tree covering nearly 1,000 square meters — is the real-world inspiration for the wisteria-covered mountain in Demon Slayer's Final Selection arc. Note: requires a detour from the main route, best as a day trip from Tokyo.

spots.name: Ookawaso Ryokan, Fukushima
spots.subtitle: The inspiration for Infinity Castle
spots.description: The tiered architecture of Ookawaso Ryokan is said to have inspired the Infinity Castle from Demon Slayer. Visitors can stay the night and soak in the onsen while surrounded by the castle-like structure. Requires a dedicated trip to Fukushima — optional but legendary.

shows.name: Naruto
shows.description: Naruto's Hidden Leaf Village (Konohagakure) draws from Japanese village architecture, Shinto shrines, and forest landscapes — all of which you'll encounter throughout the trip.

spots.name: NARUTO×BORUTO FUJI Hidden Leaf Village
spots.subtitle: The official Naruto theme park — IN YOUR ITINERARY
spots.description: The only official Hidden Leaf Village recreation in the world, located at Fuji-Q Highland in Yamanashi. You can walk through Konoha's streets, eat ramen at the real Ichiraku Ramen restaurant, take photos at the Hokage Rock monument, and play ninja games. Already on Day 4 of your itinerary.

spots.name: Naruto Museum Tokyo
spots.subtitle: Full Naruto & Boruto exhibition
spots.description: A dedicated Naruto and Boruto exhibition space in Tokyo with full story displays, original artwork, character costumes, and merchandise. Already on Day 2 of your itinerary.

spots.name: Ninja Experience Cafes (Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka)
spots.subtitle: Real ninja training & performance
spots.description: Ninja Experience Cafes in Tokyo (Harajuku/Asakusa), Kyoto, and Osaka offer actual shuriken throwing, ninja costume sessions, and theatrical performances. Perfect for Naruto fans. The Kyoto and Osaka locations are near your hotels.

shows.name: Bleach
shows.description: Bleach's Karakura Town is based on Chofu in western Tokyo, and Soul Society's aesthetic draws heavily from Kyoto's traditional architecture and Edo-period samurai culture.

spots.name: Chofu, Tokyo
spots.subtitle: The real Karakura Town
spots.description: Chofu city in western Tokyo is the confirmed real-world model for Ichigo's Karakura Town. Kurosaki Clinic's design, the shopping streets, and the residential layout all match Chofu's geography. Reachable by Keio Line from Shinjuku in 25 minutes.

spots.name: Kyoto traditional districts
spots.subtitle: Soul Society's aesthetic blueprint
spots.description: Soul Society's Seireitei — with its tiled roofs, stone walls, narrow corridors, and clan compounds — is visually based on Kyoto's traditional samurai and temple architecture. Walking through Ninen-zaka and Sannen-zaka stone-paved lanes in Kyoto feels like being in Soul Society.

spots.name: Tofuku-ji Temple, Kyoto
spots.subtitle: Grand gate that echoes the Seireitei
spots.description: Tofuku-ji's massive Sanmon gate and sweeping dry garden evoke the grand scale of Soul Society's architecture. The autumn foliage here in October is among the best in all of Kyoto. Often overlooked in favor of more famous temples — a true hidden gem.
